chains.title: Ref T allele strengthens a tumour-reprogrammed androgen receptor binding site in the 6q22 enhancer, raising RFX6
chains.cell_type: AR-positive prostate cancer cells (LNCaP clone FGC, ACH-000977)

links.claim: The only allele-specific binding statement in the evidence is for AR: rs339331 lies in an AR binding site reprogrammed in PCa tumours, with the T allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy. No QBiC-SELEX row or detail lookup for AR was provided, so coverage is not_checked; ENCODE LNCaP AR ChIP shows no peak containing the site, which may reflect absence of a matching experiment or tumour-specific (not cell-line) reprogramming.
The variant sits in a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase/H3K27ac/CTCF signal; the z-scores are maxima across biosamples, so prostate-specific activity is not demonstrated here.

RFX6 is the most likely target: the variant is intronic to RFX6, 11.7 kb from its TSS, and RFX6 is the top L2G gene (0.87) in prostate cancer credible sets. No eQTL or contact data in the evidence connect the element to RFX6, and GTEx prostate shows no significant eQTL.

An AR-dependent effect is restricted to AR-positive prostate luminal/tumour cells, the context described for the reprogrammed AR site and matching the LNCaP expression context; AR expression in ACH-000977 was not supplied.

Altered RFX6 levels are linked to prostate tumour proliferation, invasion and prognosis, and rs339331 is a genome-wide significant prostate cancer locus; note the direction conflict (GWAS effect allele C in E04 versus T risk allele in E06c) is unresolved by the evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific AR ChIP (or ChIP-qPCR) in androgen-stimulated prostate tumour material shows higher signal on T; signal is androgen-dependent.
Enzalutamide or AR knockdown abolishes the allelic reporter difference, while HOXB13 or GATA2 depletion does not.
Luciferase reporter with T versus C differs only in AR-positive, androgen-treated cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific reporter or ChIP difference persists after AR depletion/androgen deprivation.
No AR occupancy at the site in any prostate AR ChIP-seq, including tumour tissue.
C allele shows stronger AR occupancy or no allelic difference.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs339331 itself; a linked variant in the credible set carries the function
predictions: Allele-specific reporter and base-edited isogenic lines show no difference in enhancer activity or RFX6 expression.
No allelic imbalance in ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq at chr6:116888889 in heterozygous prostate samples.
Fine-mapping PIP stays low (0.06-0.23) and another credible-set SNP carries the functional signal.
falsified_if: Base editing T>C at the endogenous locus changes RFX6 expression or enhancer activity.
Reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy is shown at chr6:116888889.
Fine-mapping resolves the credible set to this SNP.

chains.title: Ref T allele creates a stronger HOXB13 site in the 6q22 enhancer, raising RFX6 in prostate tumour cells

links.claim: HOXB13 is reported to sit in a GATA2/SMAD4/HOXB13 complex at the rs339331 enhancer, but no allele-specific HOXB13 data are in the evidence (E06c's allelic statement concerns AR, not HOXB13), and ENCODE shows no HOXB13 peak containing the variant in LNCaP (which may mean no matching experiment). Coverage not checked by QBiC-SELEX. Allele assignment to T is therefore an inference, not an observation.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE, and the literature independently calls this position the '6q22 enhancer' bound by the complex.
The complex at this enhancer is reported to increase RFX6, the nearest gene and top L2G gene (0.87) in prostate cancer credible sets.
Prostate tumour cells are the stated context for this complex; HOXB13 expression in ACH-000977 was not supplied.
Higher RFX6 is associated with proliferation, invasion and poor prognosis and with prostate cancer risk at this locus.

predictions: HOXB13 ChIP in prostate cells shows a peak at chr6:116888889 with allelic imbalance toward T.
HOXB13 knockdown reduces RFX6 and abolishes the allelic reporter difference, while AR blockade does not.
T>C base editing lowers RFX6 without changing GPRC6A.
falsified_if: No HOXB13 occupancy at the site in any prostate HOXB13 ChIP-seq.
C allele binds HOXB13 more, or no allelic difference in HOXB13 binding.
RFX6 is unchanged by HOXB13 depletion in prostate cells.

chains.title: GATA2 is the allele-sensitive factor at the 6q22 enhancer, driving RFX6 through the GATA2/SMAD4/HOXB13 complex
chains.cell_type: Prostate cancer cells with TGFbeta1/SMAD4 signalling (LNCaP)

links.claim: GATA2 is named as part of the complex at the rs339331 enhancer; the evidence gives no GATA2 allele-specific binding data and does not identify GATA2 as the pioneer factor, so T-allele preference is assumed, not shown. No QBiC-SELEX lookup for GATA2 was available (not_checked).
The complex is placed at the rs339331/6q22 enhancer, which coincides with the dELS cCRE containing the variant.
The complex is reported to increase expression of the susceptibility gene RFX6, which also has the highest L2G score.
Prostate tumour cells with GATA2/SMAD4 activity are the described context; co-expression in LNCaP was not shown in the evidence.
Increased RFX6 modulates prostate cancer progression, consistent with the strong GWAS association at rs339331.

predictions: GATA2 knockdown collapses enhancer activity and RFX6 more than HOXB13 or AR depletion.
TGFbeta1 stimulation amplifies the allelic difference via SMAD4 recruitment.
GATA2 ChIP shows allelic imbalance toward T in heterozygotes.
falsified_if: No GATA2 occupancy or motif at the variant.
GATA2 depletion leaves RFX6 and enhancer activity intact.
SMAD4/TGFbeta perturbation does not modulate the allelic effect.

chains.title: Same enhancer, different target: allele-dependent binding alters GPRC6A rather than RFX6
chains.element: EH38E2496909 dELS, SCREEN-linked to RFX6, GPRC6A and FAM162B

links.claim: Binding follows the only allele-specific statement available (AR, stronger on T); coverage not checked, and no LNCaP AR peak contains the site.
The cCRE's SCREEN gene assignment is proximity-based and lists GPRC6A and FAM162B alongside RFX6, so the target is not fixed by this evidence.

GPRC6A is 59.8 kb away and receives modest L2G support (0.05-0.16 in the sets shown, best 0.38), far below RFX6 (0.87); no contact or eQTL evidence supports it, and prostate eQTL analysis is null for both genes.
Prostate epithelial cells are the assumed context; no evidence of GPRC6A expression in prostate or LNCaP was provided.
The locus also associates with small-HDL lipid traits, which is at least compatible with a non-RFX6 effector, though no evidence ties these traits to GPRC6A.

predictions: CRISPRi of the enhancer in LNCaP changes GPRC6A more than RFX6.
Chromatin-contact data place the element at the GPRC6A promoter.
Any eQTL that emerges in larger prostate datasets is for GPRC6A, not RFX6.
falsified_if: No physical contact between the element and the GPRC6A promoter.
GPRC6A is not expressed in prostate epithelium or LNCaP.

grades_v0.reason: E06d shows HOXB13 in a complex at the rs339331 enhancer, but it gives no allele-specific HOXB13 data. E06c reports T-allele enhanced occupancy for AR, not HOXB13. The claim borrows AR's allelic result for HOXB13. No QBiC or ChIP evidence was supplied.

E03 places the variant inside dELS EH38E2496909 with DNase and H3K27ac signal. These are maxima over biosamples, not LNCaP-specific, so prostate activity is not shown. E06d independently places the complex at the rs339331 enhancer.

E05 gives L2G of 0.87 for RFX6 and E02 shows it is the nearest gene. E06d states the complex leads to increased RFX6 expression. This is genetic plus literature support, though no direct perturbation or eQTL of the element was shown.
E06c and E06d describe prostate tumours and PCa cells, but neither quote names LNCaP or luminal cells. No expression data for HOXB13, GATA2 or AR in ACH-000977 were provided.

E04 shows a strong GWAS association (p 5e-20) and E06a/E06e link RFX6 to tumour behaviour. Direction is only partly consistent: C is the GWAS effect allele, yet E06c says T is the risk allele. The effect of RFX6 on risk via this variant is not demonstrated, and the prediction that editing T>C lowers RFX6 is untested.

E06c directly states that rs339331 lies in a reprogrammed AR binding site with the T risk allele enhancing AR occupancy. This is a literature statement of allele-specific occupancy, which is better than a prediction. The primary data are not shown, and the T risk allele conflicts with E04 listing C as the GWAS effect allele.
E03 supports a dELS with open chromatin and H3K27ac, but values are biosample maxima and not specific to prostate or AR sites. The AR site assignment rests on E06c alone.

E01 and E05 support RFX6 as the likely gene. E06b only reports the locus association. No evidence shows AR regulates RFX6 through this element. Citing E06d's RFX6 upregulation would concern the GATA2/HOXB13 complex rather than AR.

E06c mentions PCa tumours with a reprogrammed AR site, which is consistent with AR-positive cells. LNCaP is not named, no AR expression was supplied, and the claim that the effect requires AR signalling is untested.

The claim that RFX6 is induced by AR to promote progression and drug resistance via HOXA10/TGFb relies on the title of PMID 38932472 in E06, which is not quoted. E06a and E06b are general. The PSA association in E04 has effect allele T, whereas the PCa effect allele is C, so the direction needs reconciling and is not shown to track AR output.

E06d shows GATA2/SMAD4/HOXB13 complex formation at the enhancer. Nothing states that GATA2 is the pioneer factor or that its occupancy is allele-dependent. E06c concerns AR. The pioneer and allele-dependence claims are unsupported inventions.
E06d places the complex at the rs339331/6q22 enhancer and E03 shows the variant lies within a dELS cCRE. The match is consistent, though biosample-specific activity is not shown.
E06d directly states that the complex leads to increased expression of RFX6, and E05 gives L2G 0.87 for RFX6. This is the strongest gene link of the chains.
E06d implies prostate cancer cells for the complex, but co-expression of GATA2, SMAD4 and HOXB13 in tumour cells or LNCaP is not shown. TGFb1 signalling activity in LNCaP is not evidenced.

E04 and E06b give a strong GWAS signal and E06a links RFX6 to progression. The route from the GATA2 complex to risk via RFX6 is an inference. The chain is partly redundant with H1 and offers no evidence separating GATA2 from HOXB13.
The claim that HOXB13 binds with stronger T-allele occupancy is not supported by E06d or E06c. E06c concerns AR, and E06d shows the complex but no allelic data.
E03 lists GPRC6A among nearby genes, but this is only proximity-based assignment. It does not show that the element targets GPRC6A. The same E03 line lists RFX6 first.
GPRC6A has L2G of only 0.05 to 0.16 in the sets shown (best 0.38 across all sets), far below RFX6 at 0.87. E06d directly implicates RFX6. Being 59.8 km away is not evidence of regulation.
E05 contains nothing about GPRC6A expression in prostate epithelium or LNCaP, nor about androgen or osteocalcin responsiveness. The claim is from outside knowledge.
E04 lists lipid/HDL associations but does not tie them to GPRC6A. No evidence links GPRC6A to prostate tumour growth. The claim that RFX6 does not explain the HDL signal is speculation.

grades_final.reason: E06c directly states rs339331 lies in a reprogrammed AR site with the T risk allele enhancing AR occupancy, which matches allele_binding_more=ref. This comes from allelic literature evidence, not a SELEX prediction. E08 shows no LNCaP AR peak, but the absence is non-informative. Coverage is not_checked; suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for AR. The E04 C-effect-allele direction conflict is unresolved.

E03 shows a dELS cCRE containing the variant, and E06c places it in an AR binding site. However the z-scores are maxima over biosamples and no prostate- or LNCaP-specific activity is shown. E01 reports no regulatory feature.

Support is intronic position, 11.7 kb to the RFX6 TSS, and L2G 0.87 (E05), which is genetic colocalisation-style prioritisation rather than perturbation. E06d reports the enhancer increases RFX6, but that concerns the GATA2/HOXB13 complex rather than AR. GTEx prostate eQTL is null (E09), and no contact or CRISPR data are given.

E06c places the AR site in PCa tumours, which is consistent with AR-positive prostate cells. LNCaP AR expression was not shown, and E08 shows no AR peak in LNCaP. Only tumour-context literature supports this link.

E04 and E06b show a strong prostate cancer GWAS association, and E06a links RFX6 dysregulation to tumour phenotypes. But E06a is a generic review statement, not tied to this variant. The direction is inconsistent: E04 effect allele C versus the T risk allele in E06c. The link from AR-driven RFX6 change to the phenotype is not shown.

E06d places HOXB13 in a complex at the rs339331 enhancer, but no HOXB13 allele-specific data exist. E06c concerns AR, not HOXB13. E07 shows no LNCaP peak, which is uninformative. The T-allele preference is an inference. Coverage is not_checked; suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for HOXB13.
E03 shows a dELS cCRE containing the variant, and E06d independently calls this position the rs339331/6q22 enhancer bound by the complex.

E06d states the complex at this enhancer increases RFX6 expression, and E05 gives L2G 0.87 with E02 giving proximity. The literature quote is only a summary and not directly a perturbation shown here. E09 prostate eQTL is null, and the effect is attributed to the complex rather than to HOXB13 allele-specific binding.
E06d gives prostate tumour context for the complex. HOXB13 expression in LNCaP/ACH-000977 was not supplied, so it is only consistent with the claim.

E04, E06b, E06a and E06e link the locus and RFX6 to prostate cancer risk and progression, but E06a and E06e are generic. The allele and direction chain through HOXB13 is unresolved, with an E04 C versus T risk conflict. E06e is an association with RFX6, not directional evidence.

E06d only names GATA2 as part of a complex at the enhancer. No GATA2 allele-specific data are given and the T preference is assumed. E06c concerns AR. Coverage is not_checked; suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for GATA2.
E06d places the complex at the rs339331/6q22 enhancer, and E03 shows the variant lies in a dELS cCRE at that position.

E06d reports increased RFX6 expression from the complex at this enhancer, and E05 gives the top L2G of 0.87. It is a literature statement, not data shown here, and it is not specific to GATA2 allele binding. No eQTL support is shown (E09 null).
E06d gives prostate cancer context with GATA2/SMAD4, but LNCaP co-expression was not shown and no ACH-000977 evidence was cited.

E04 and E06b support a locus-level prostate cancer association, and E06a links RFX6 to progression generically. Nothing ties a GATA2-specific allelic mechanism to the phenotype, and the E04 effect-allele C versus T risk direction is not reconciled.

The AR statement in E06c supports T-allele AR binding at the site, but it is linked to RFX6 in the literature, not GPRC6A. E08 shows no LNCaP peak, which is uninformative. Coverage is not_checked; suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup for AR.
E03 shows a dELS cCRE containing the variant, with nearby genes RFX6, GPRC6A and FAM162B listed by proximity only. This does not establish GPRC6A as the target of the element.

The evidence points to RFX6, not GPRC6A. E05 gives L2G of 0.05-0.16 for GPRC6A (best 0.38) versus 0.87 for RFX6, and E06d links the enhancer to increased RFX6. There is no contact or eQTL support for GPRC6A, and E09 is null. GPRC6A at 59.8 kb is only a proximity candidate.
No evidence was cited, and the link states that GPRC6A expression in prostate or LNCaP was not provided.
E04 lists small-HDL lipid associations, but nothing ties them or prostate cancer to GPRC6A. The claim is speculative and conflicts with the prostate cancer disease context.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs339331 resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.

Strinkingly, GATA2 and SMAD4 globally mediated inherited PCa risk and formed a transcriptional complex with HOXB13 at the PCa risk-associated rs339331/6q22 enhancer, leading to increased expression of the PCa susceptibility gene RFX6.
Notable genes of interest include HCP5, RFX6 and H3C1 for risk, and MKI67 and KLF5 for aggressive disease.
